draft.subject: Five minutes to set up, zero migration
draft.body:
Jordan,

Documentation adds up fast when you're working with clients all day.

JotPsych writes structured behavioral health notes from your session audio — on any device, in real time. Pre-built templates, or upload your own. No EHR change required.

You can add it to whatever system you use now. No migration, no IT project, up in five minutes. When you're ready, it can become the whole practice: notes, scheduling, billing, e-prescribing, telehealth.

Over 10,000 behavioral health practices use it. 2.5M+ notes written. HIPAA compliant.

If you want to see it again, I'll set up a quick walkthrough. Or you can start a trial directly at jotpsych.com.

Thanks,

[Name]
JotPsych

--
You are receiving this because you signed up for JotPsych.
To stop receiving these, reply with the word STOP.
JotPsych, Brooklyn Navy Yard, Dock 72, 7th Floor, Brooklyn, NY 11205
claims: JotPsych writes structured behavioral health notes from session audio
Allows users to upload their own templates
No EHR change required to add JotPsych
Can be set up in five minutes
Can become the whole practice when ready
Includes notes, scheduling, billing, e-prescribing, telehealth
Over 10,000 behavioral health practices use JotPsych

failures: unfilled placeholder / template artifact left in the draft

judge: The email describes JotPsych primarily as a documentation/note-taking tool ('JotPsych writes structured behavioral health notes from your session audio') when the FACT PACK explicitly states: 'It is no longer positioned as a scribe bolted onto someone else's EHR. It is the EHR. Writing to a clinician as if it were only a note-taker is wrong.'

judge: The email omits JotPsych's core differentiator entirely. The FACT PACK states the current positioning is 'the behavioral health EHR that defends you from insurance companies' with '150+ payer rules' checked per note and claim. None of this appears in the draft.

judge: The recipient's specialty is 'Behavior Technician' (from allowed_facts), not a prescriber or licensed clinician who would typically manage 'clients,' use an EHR, or handle e-prescribing. The email assumes clinical responsibilities that may not match this role.
judge: The phrase 'working with clients all day' makes an assumption about the recipient's practice pattern that is not in the RECIPIENT RECORD.
